entries.name: Connectivity Index (migratory species)
entries.definition: Structured, evidence-based connectivity profile for a DA-validated shortlist of highly migratory and/or vulnerable taxa (cetaceans, seabirds, elasmobranchs): cross-area occurrence, recurrence and seasonality, and stepping-stone plausibility. A connectivity proxy, not an abundance, density or trend estimate.

S1.magnitude_text: No improvements in seasonal coupling between islands and pelagic zones

S2.magnitude_text: Slight improvements from better data alignment; seasonal presence described more consistently between islands

S3.magnitude_text: Where baseline shows recurrence or seasonality, coordinated management across islands becomes feasible

S4.magnitude_text: S3 improvements remain, with added value from reduced edge effects beyond EEZ boundaries

early_warning.trigger: Seasonal presence is recorded differently or managed inconsistently across islands; timing confusion for users and managers
Offshore use is documented, but no linked management exists; 'paper corridor' critique emerges
One archipelago takes action while others lag, or gear/use rules differ for same species
Discrepancy in enforcement effort, rules, or communication across agencies
Stakeholder feedback flags corridor as symbolic, unfair, or externally imposed; pushback slows uptake

Scenario direction_text is the near-island (EEZ) column of Table 3 (0/+/++/+++ ordinal legend). Criterion roles are taken from the interpretation bridge (L10823-10835) because the Table 1 role column interleaves in the extract.

entries.name: Pelagic (tuna) landing share
entries.definition: Share of tuna in total commercial landings per archipelago, from aggregated landings (t) of five highly migratory tuna species; 3-year rolling average.

early_warning.lever: Leakage and displacement management are the hinge.
Substitute fisheries must be part of the story.

data_sources: Regional fisheries landings statistics (Madeira, Azores, Canaries)
entries.caveat: Scenario directions are the 'Expected ΔF_02' column of 'Table 1 Scenario-based assumptions' (L11271-11313); the prose below it (L11317) calls the same table 'Table 2'. The landings-bound columns interleave in the layout, so magnitude_text is left null.
source_quotes: Corridor design implications (as indicated by F_02)
Leakage and displacement management are the hinge.

entries.name: CPUE: catch per unit effort
entries.definition: Catch rate of selected key species relevant to the corridor (primarily highly migratory pelagics), as catch (number or weight) per standardised unit of fishing effort (e.g. kg per set; fish per 1,000 hooks; t per fishing hour/day).

S1.magnitude_text: More of the same: noisy year-to-year swings; any trend is slow and hard to attribute

S2.magnitude_text: Slightly calmer signal possible: less erratic CPUE, small stabilisation at best

S3.magnitude_text: Patchy results: some places/fleets report CPUE up, others down

S4.magnitude_text: Best chance of a consistent stabilisation signal; early adjustment turbulence still likely

data_sources: Fishery-dependent catch and effort data (logbooks), standardised per species and fleet/gear segment
entries.caveat: D5.2 describes the CPUE baseline method (L11653-11695) but publishes no CPUE values. The EQ row of the criteria table is printed twice (L11648-11651); it is recorded once.
source_quotes: Indicator F_03 - CPUE: Catch per Unit Effort
Establish baseline CPUE values for selected species

entries.definition: Register- or licence-based counts by archipelago and segment: commercial fishing vessels by home port / operational base (F_04a) and licensed recreational fishing charter operators and/or vessels (F_04b), separated to avoid double counting.

S1.magnitude_text: Background variability dominates (fuel, weather, markets); tourism seasonality dominates; corridor signal absent

S2.magnitude_text: Slight predictability gain (fewer rule surprises); limited cost change

S3.magnitude_text: Re-targeting and crowding: shifts in grounds/species; higher time/fuel/admin

S4.magnitude_text: Two-track outcome: stabilisation if credible coherence reduces leakage; otherwise, burden dominates

early_warning.metric: evidence of consistent enforcement; leakage narratives; rule 'work-arounds'

early_warning.lever: Equity safeguards (proportionate requirements; targeted transition support)

entries.name: Number of vessel movements between islands
entries.definition: Frequency of vessel transits between the Azores, Madeira and the Canary Islands over a year.
entries.caveat: The baseline table caption in the source reads 'Number of marine tourism companies' (copy-paste error); the rows are vessel counts. The criteria table header reads 'Use of T_03' (A§5.1). Madeira-Canaries data not available. Magnitude cells are assigned in PDF reading order (p. 300).

S1.assumption_text: Stable or gradually increasing vessel movements
S1.magnitude_text: Unmanaged overlap with migratory routes; persistent pressure

S2.assumption_text: Branding activities leading to awareness effects
S2.magnitude_text: Improved awareness improves, but quantity mainly unchanged

S3.assumption_text: Routing adjustment, slow-down areas in limited areas
S3.magnitude_text: Traffic influenced by routing and spatial management

S4.assumption_text: Routing measures and potentially binding obligations in high-risk areas
S4.magnitude_text: Strongest reduction in high-risk movements; structured connectivity

source_quotes: Number of vessel movements between islands

entries.name: Total visitors
entries.definition: Number of non-resident visitors arriving in the corridor-affected territories of Macaronesia (Azores, Madeira, Canary Islands) per year; covers all tourism, not only marine tourism.

S1.assumption_text: Growth driven by market forces; no corridor signal

S2.assumption_text: Positive branding effect without regulatory costs
S2.magnitude_text: Remain at least stable relative to S1, potentially increase slightly due to enhanced destination image

S3.assumption_text: Adjustment phase followed by quality-driven growth
S3.magnitude_text: Short-term stabilisation, medium-term moderate growth especially in nature tourism

S4.assumption_text: Possible volume stabilisation; shift to high-value tourism
S4.magnitude_text: Slower growth, stable (less) mass tourism, more high-value tourism

data_sources: Regional statistics offices (Azores, Madeira, Canary Islands), annual non-resident visitors
entries.caveat: The criteria table header reads 'Use of F_04' (copy-paste error). 2024 data for the Canary Islands were not available at the time of analysis. Magnitude cells are assigned in reading order (same layout as the M_01 synthesis table).

entries.name: Number of marine tourism companies
entries.alt_meaning: Shortlist meaning: wildlife-watch participation (A§5.1); fiche meaning is canonical pending partner Q3
entries.definition: Count of active, licensed businesses offering marine tourism services (whale-watching, diving, tourist fishing, leisure boat hire and other nature-based marine activities) in the Macaronesian archipelagos.

S1.assumption_text: Sector expansion, without a corresponding corridor mechanism to steer behavior
S1.magnitude_text: Continuation of current development, unmanaged expansion

S2.assumption_text: Voluntary and soft governance mechanisms are implemented, voluntary codes, branding
S2.magnitude_text: Growth continues; early professionalization via voluntary standards

S3.magnitude_text: Slower growth; consolidation and regulated capacity in sensitive areas

S4.magnitude_text: Strongest shift toward high-standard and lower-impact operator base

entries.caveat: Comparable data for the Canary Islands were not available. Synthesis cells read in PDF reading order (p. 314).
